evidence.detail: load_matches called with where='m.id IN (...)' only — no constraint on which deck becomes d (person/hero); GROUP BY m.id makes MySQL pick arbitrarily
GROUP BY m.id comment: 'We don't want a row for each deck in a match (when the WHERE doesn't include a person)' — confirms non-determinism when no person filter
hero_deck_ids are known at this point and used to load hero_decks — they can be reused in the match WHERE clause to pin d to the hero side

triage.fix_sketch: In decksite/data/matchup.py line 80, change the match WHERE clause to: `where='m.id IN (' + ', '.join(match_ids) + ') AND d.id IN (' + ', '.join(hero_deck_ids) + ')'`. This ensures the hero deck is always d (left/person side) in the match display. No other files need changing.
triage.notes: The hero_deck_ids list is already available at the match-loading call site; this is a 1-line change to the WHERE string. The GROUP BY m.id in load_matches already deduplicates so no extra rows appear.
